scope: Fresh bounded display-pixel review of exactly six existing English N88 desktop/mobile captures; PASS applies only to the visible layout and figure framing within this evidence.
imageBindingProvenance: Exact image paths, byte counts and SHA-256 bindings transcribed from the hash-verified display report. Each named image was inspected once with view_image; image hashes were not independently recomputed.

observations: The whole lesson is visibly populated from the title and breadcrumb through the final paragraph. A centered single reading column has consistent paragraph spacing and three visible section separators.

Figure 169 appears between its introducing prose and the following prose, with a separate centered caption and clear surrounding whitespace. No gross content/figure overlap, horizontal clipping, truncated page ending, or blank figure rendering is visible.
The whole-page preview was resized from 1440x8195 to 1054x6000. This observation establishes overall layout, not exhaustive fine-glyph readability.

The unscaled viewport visibly shows the lesson opening: title, breadcrumb, the first section label and initial prose. These visible glyphs are legible, with distinct lines, paragraph gaps and unobstructed margins.
Despite its filename, this capture shows the opening viewport, not a separate polarization-definition region. No additional region-specific readability approval is inferred.
Prose continuing below the screenshot's bottom edge is ordinary viewport continuation, not evidence of lesson-container clipping.

images.widthProvenance: views[0].geometry.figures[0] and the bound width result
observations: At the report-bound 640 px media width, the complete arch, both lower ends and all exterior arrow tips are inside the image with whitespace around the extremities. Lines and arrowheads are clearly distinguishable; rendering is nonblank and not visibly stretched.

No textual labels are visible inside this figure capture. Arrowheads are legible graphical marks, not textual-label evidence. The Figure 169 caption is visible in the whole-page capture outside the dedicated figure image.
The complete narrow lesson column is visibly populated from the wrapped title and breadcrumb to the final paragraph. Section separators remain distinct, and prose stays within the side margins.

Figure 169 occupies the column between its introducing and following prose, with a separate centered caption. No gross overflow, overlapping paragraph blocks, figure occlusion, blank media area, or truncated final block is visible.
The whole-page preview was resized from 390x12132 to 193x6000. Its small glyphs and caption cannot support native-size fine-text certification across the full mobile lesson.
The unscaled opening viewport has a clean two-line title, a separately wrapped breadcrumb and readable initial section/prose text inside the 358 px reading column of the 390 px viewport.
Visible text does not collide with neighboring lines or the side margins. Paragraph spacing remains clear, and no missing-glyph boxes or blank text rendering are visible in this capture.

As on desktop, the filename does not establish coverage of a polarization-definition region: the displayed pixels are the lesson opening. Text continuing below the viewport is not a container-clipping defect.

images.widthProvenance: views[1].geometry.figures[0] and the bound width result
observations: At the report-bound 358 px media width, the full arch, lower ends and exterior arrow tips remain within the image. The nested strokes and arrowheads remain distinguishable, with no visible clipping, blank rendering or aspect-ratio distortion.
No textual labels are visible within this figure image, so no in-figure font-size or label-readability certification is made. The whole-page caption is visible but downscaled.

acceptedPriorScope.provenance: User-supplied approved scope, with object/paragraph/exercise counts corroborated by the allowed report. Not independently reconstructed from source.
acceptedPriorScope.figureReuseEvidence: The allowed width result records unchanged source geometry, English figure labels and approved SVG bytes; original-source figure review is reused, not repeated.

limitations: PASS is restricted to these six existing captures and their report-bound desktop/mobile layout; it is not full-course content, scientific correctness or original-source fidelity approval.

Very tall whole screenshots were automatically downscaled by the image viewer. Whole-page observations cover overall flow, spacing, placement and gross clipping/overlap only, not every glyph, mathematical mark, footnote or caption at native scale.

Fine-glyph readability observations apply only to text actually visible in the unscaled opening viewport captures. The polarization filenames do not provide independent pixels of another definition region.

The dedicated figure captures contain no textual labels. Visible arrows and strokes are distinguishable at the reported 640/358 px widths, but no nonexistent labels or numeric minimum-font threshold are certified.
Actual media widths are taken from the hash-verified existing DOM/display and width-result evidence; no new measurement, render or browser run was performed.

Chinese machine ARIA and source identities remain retained and disclosed, including the reported figure ARIA label. No complete English accessibility approval, screen-reader testing or identity translation is claimed.
Evidence is isolated offline headless display, not headed product verification, production acceptance or interaction testing.
